pages.title: What it does
text: It drives the vanilla minecraft:max_health attribute, raising your maximum health.

When the maximum rises, max_health.heal_mode decides what happens to your current health: ADD_DELTA (default) grants as much health as the maximum gained, KEEP_RATIO preserves the ratio and NONE grants nothing.
Death and respawn never cost you stats: level, experience, points and every allocation are kept.

pages.title: Flat (numeric) line
text: The curve is LINEAR: +1 health per point (half a heart), with no ceiling.
A player's base maximum health is 20.0 (10 hearts).

pages.title: Percent line
text: Also LINEAR: +2% per point, on the TOTAL basis.
TOTAL means the percentage scales base 20.0 + any health your equipment contributes (vanilla has none) + the result of the flat line.
Worked example: 20 flat + 20 percent -> (20 + 20) * (1 + 40%) = 56.0 max health.

pages.title: Ceiling & returns
text: There is no designed functional ceiling (this mod does not cap it); both lines are linear.

The only boundary is the attribute's own range: vanilla clamps max_health at 1024 (= 512 hearts). About 1004 flat points, or about 2510 percent points, reach it. Past that further points do nothing and the row shows a "!" marker. An attribute-range mod (AttributeFix) raises that boundary automatically.
With diminishing returns gone everywhere, it remains the most purely linear dimension: a constant return per point, stacking forever.

pages.title: Practical advice
text: Health is forgiveness, not mitigation: it keeps you alive through mistakes, but a big hit still takes a big bite. Combine it with damage reduction and health regeneration for a complete defensive build.
The first 20..40 points are excellent value (10..20 hearts of buffer).
Note that ADD_DELTA mode heals you as you allocate; that is intended behaviour, not a bug.
